images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of the shared-control maze environment.The agent-controlled avatar (blue) and human-controlled avatar (orange) share the objective of reaching the target (green). At each team turn, the model selects one of three action types: (1) move its own avatar, (2) allocate the move to the human with a directional recommendation, or (3) hand the move over without a recommendation. The model receives the global maze topology and both avatar positions, depicted schematically here, whereas the human acts from a local view. Initial avatar positions vary the relative shortest-path advantage of the agent and human.

Figure 2:Initial self-action by assigned route advantage.Points show the initial self-action rate (ISR) under AI-shorter (Δ0=−2\Delta_{0}=-2), equal-route (Δ0=0\Delta_{0}=0), and human-shorter (Δ0=+2\Delta_{0}=+2) starting conditions. Error bars show 95% two-way cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals over participants and maze seeds. Each model–condition cell contains 40 episodes. The dashed horizontal line marks a descriptive reference value of 0.5.

Figure 3:Action allocation by current relative route advantage.Columns correspond to models, and rows group observed turns according to whether the Agent-controlled avatar has the shorter current route, the two routes are equal, or the human-controlled avatar has the shorter current route. Pie slices show the Current-state action rate (CAR) of self-action, guidance, and deference within each model–advantage cell. Current route advantage is evaluated immediately before each model decision.
